title: Metallic Structure — Oversize Hole and Plug Repair Practice

issue.reason: Original issue of the oversize hole and interference plug practice for metallic structure.

abstract: The standard practice for restoring a mis-drilled or elongated fastener hole in metallic structure, by reaming to an oversize dimension or by installing an interference plug and re-drilling.

sections.purpose: This practice gives the two accepted methods for restoring a fastener hole in metallic structure that has been mis-drilled, elongated in service or damaged during fastener removal.
sections.damage_assessment: Measure the hole at three angular positions with the bore gauge and record the largest and the smallest diameter; an elongated hole is identified by the difference between the two rather than by the largest value alone. Establish the edge distance to the nearest free edge and to the neighbouring hole, because the oversize method reduces both and the plug method does not. Where the hole is in a fatigue-critical location identified in the applicable structure repair section, the oversize method may not be used at all. Record the parent material and its thickness, because the plug interference fit depends on both. A hole whose largest diameter exceeds twice nominal is outside this practice and needs an engineering assessment.
sections.repair_procedure: For the oversize method, ream the hole in one operation to the next oversize dimension in the table on repair drawing RD-51-70-11-908, using a piloted reamer and cutting fluid, and do not step through intermediate sizes. Deburr both faces, do an eddy current inspection of the reamed bore and confirm the edge distance still meets the minimum for the oversize fastener. Install the oversize fastener wet with sealant. For the plug method, ream the hole to the plug interference dimension, cool the plug D5170111191879 to the temperature given on the drawing and press it in within the time window stated. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the plug periphery on both faces after the plug has reached ambient temperature. Re-drill the original hole position through the plug, deburr and do an eddy current inspection of the new bore. Install the standard fastener; use rivets AGS611113-6C where the joint is riveted and swaged collars EN923552-9E where it is not. Apply the surface protection of ATA 51-20 to all disturbed surfaces and record the method, the final hole size and the fastener used on the aircraft structural record sheet.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of every repaired hole at the next scheduled structural inspection of the area. Where the oversize method has been used in a joint that carries a repeat inspection, that inspection continues at its existing interval and is not relaxed. Not more than three adjacent holes in one fastener row may be repaired by either method, and not more than one may use the plug method. Report a plug repair to Aeralis; an oversize repair inside the table limits does not need to be reported.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Holes whose largest diameter does not exceed twice nominal, with the edge distance after repair not less than two times the final fastener diameter. Not more than three adjacent holes in one fastener row, of which not more than one may use the plug method.

title: Metallic Structure — Oversize Hole and Plug Repair Practice

issue.reason: Edge distance to a machined pocket corner added to the assessment and plug repair near a corner made subject to concession.

abstract: The standard practice for restoring a mis-drilled or elongated fastener hole in metallic structure, by reaming to an oversize dimension or by installing an interference plug, with the exclusions that apply at sealed lands, shear tie joints and machined pockets.

sections.purpose: This practice gives the two accepted methods for restoring a fastener hole in metallic structure that has been mis-drilled, elongated in service or damaged during fastener removal.
sections.damage_assessment: Measure the hole at three angular positions with the bore gauge and record the largest and the smallest diameter; an elongated hole is identified by the difference between the two rather than by the largest value alone. Establish the edge distance to the nearest free edge and to the neighbouring hole, because the oversize method reduces both and the plug method does not. In a web that carries machined relief, take the edge distance to the nearest pocket corner as well; the corner radius is the governing free edge there and it is usually closer than the panel boundary the table assumes. Where the hole is in a fatigue-critical location identified in the applicable structure repair section, the oversize method may not be used at all. Establish whether the hole lies in the bolted joint of a two-piece aft engine mount shear tie; that joint carries mount shear directly across the plug plane and no plug interference fit is qualified against it. Record the parent material and its thickness, because the plug interference fit depends on both. A hole whose largest diameter exceeds twice nominal is outside this practice and needs an engineering assessment.
sections.repair_procedure: For the oversize method, ream the hole in one operation to the next oversize dimension in the table on repair drawing RD-51-70-11-908, using a piloted reamer and cutting fluid, and do not step through intermediate sizes. Deburr both faces, do an eddy current inspection of the reamed bore and confirm the edge distance still meets the minimum for the oversize fastener. Install the oversize fastener wet with sealant. For the plug method, ream the hole to the plug interference dimension, cool the plug D5170111191879 to the temperature given on the drawing and press it in within the time window stated. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the plug periphery on both faces after the plug has reached ambient temperature. Re-drill the original hole position through the plug, deburr and do an eddy current inspection of the new bore. Install the standard fastener; use rivets AGS611113-6C where the joint is riveted and swaged collars EN923552-9E where it is not. Where the repaired land afterwards carries a continuous sealant bead, terminate the bead not less than one plug diameter clear of the plug on both sides and close the interruption with a brush coat of the same material; a bead run straight across a plugged and re-protected land is not qualified and must not be laid. Do not plug a hole in the bolted joint of a two-piece aft engine mount shear tie under any circumstances without a written design office concession, including where the hole is inside the table limits. Apply the surface protection of ATA 51-20 to all disturbed surfaces and record the method, the final hole size and the fastener used on the aircraft structural record sheet.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a detailed visual inspection of every repaired hole at the next scheduled structural inspection of the area. Where the oversize method has been used in a joint that carries a repeat inspection, that inspection continues at its existing interval and is not relaxed. Before any embodiment that lays a continuous sealant bead along a land repaired under this practice, read the plug population of that land off the aircraft repair file and record it on the work package, so that the bead can be set out around the plugs at the aircraft. A plug installed within one and a half plug diameters of a machined pocket corner is reportable in every case and is subject to a design office concession before the work starts. Not more than three adjacent holes in one fastener row may be repaired by either method, and not more than one may use the plug method. Report a plug repair to Aeralis; an oversize repair inside the table limits does not need to be reported.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Holes whose largest diameter does not exceed twice nominal, with the edge distance after repair not less than two times the final fastener diameter, measured to the nearest pocket corner where the web is machined. Not more than three adjacent holes in one fastener row, of which not more than one may use the plug method. A plug in a land that is to carry a continuous sealant bead is acceptable only with the bead terminated clear of the plug. The bolted joint of a two-piece aft engine mount shear tie is excluded from the plug method, and a plug within one and a half plug diameters of a pocket corner needs a concession.
